best_for: People who download large files, torrents or many links at once and want one free manager that catches downloads from Chrome, Firefox or Edge.

points.title: Free, but not open source
points.text: FDM is free of charge and the site promises no adware or spyware. It is closed-source freeware, and Flathub lists its license as proprietary.

points.title: Torrents are built in
points.text: A BitTorrent client is part of the app, with magnet links, per-download priority and bandwidth control. You do not need a second program for torrents.

points.title: Browser catch needs the extension
points.text: FDM can take over downloads from Chrome, Firefox and Edge. The site says the official extension is needed for the best browser integration.

points.title: Video sites need an add-on
points.text: Downloading video from web pages comes from a separate add-on hosted on GitHub, not from the core app.

points.title: Older systems have their own builds
points.text: Current FDM needs Windows 10 or 11. The site still offers 6.24 for Windows 7, 8 and 8.1 and for macOS 10.12 to 11, and 6.30.3 for macOS 12.

points.title: A verified Flatpak, x64 only
points.text: The Flatpak is marked verified on Flathub, so it comes from the FDM team. It is built for x64 only. The site also offers a .deb.

points.title: Choose per-user or machine-wide
points.text: The Windows installer comes in per-user and machine-wide forms, and macOS has separate Intel and Apple silicon disk images. Windows keeps 2 versions here; macOS and Linux list only the current release.
